title: Capacitor threshold probe: microburst absorption notes
content:
Quick context and intent:
- This is a personal scratchpad for an experiment that treats the request ingress pipeline like an electrical capacitor: can the system 'absorb' short microbursts without violating p99 SLOs by tuning a few knobs (prefill, soft-hold, drain-rate).
- Goal: find a simple, low-risk set of config patches we can recommend for Dedicated pools to smooth 50–200 qps spikes lasting 50–1000ms.
- Not attempting full theory; heuristics + empirical numbers for ops-runbook.

Hypothesis (informal):
- If we maintain a small in-memory prefix cache + prefill budget (token-capacitor) sized to typical burst size, the serving runtime can amortize KV warmups and avoid p99 amplifications.
- There is a sweet spot where absorption reduces p99 by >=30% for short bursts without raising median latency by >10% under steady traffic.

Experiment design (end-to-end):
1) Workload generator: local injector that can replay production-ish arrival traces (zipfian + short heavy tails). Use synthetic waveforms: single-pulse, shear-wave, and damped-oscillation.
2) Target model: quantized-7B-llama-variant on a single GPU in Dedicated dev pool (same as DEV-GPU-3). Keep KV-cache enabled.
3) Baseline config: default batching (max_batch_tokens=2048, batch_timeout_ms=8), no prefill, no soft-hold.
4) Treatments: two knobs:
   - prefill_budget_tokens: [0, 512, 2048]
   - soft_hold_ms: [0, 10, 40] (soft_hold = delay before launching new batch to allow in-flight cache priming to serve later requests)
   - drain_rate_factor: [1.0, 0.8] (throttle output encoding frequency to simulate slower drains)
5) Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (full generation), KV-cache hit rate, batch sizes distribution, tokens/sec per GPU, tail amplification factor (p99/p50).

Commands and infra notes (for reproducibility):
- injector: ./tools/injector --pattern=shear --qps=150 --pulse-width-ms=200 --duration=60000 --clients=120 --payload=prompt-short.json
- server: dev-dedicated-1 (g4dn-like) run pinned branch: dev/capacitor-probe (PR 582)
- perf traces: /tmp/cap-probe/run-<treatment>-<ts>.jsonl (contains per-request trace ids and timestamps)

Key raw observations (representative runs):
- Baseline (0 prefill, 0 soft_hold) shear pulse qps=150/200ms pulse:
  p50=45ms, p95=220ms, p99=780ms, kv-hit=12%, median batch=2
  note: p99 driven by cold KV warms + many tiny batches.

- Treatment A (prefill=512, soft_hold=10ms):
  p50=48ms, p95=160ms, p99=500ms, kv-hit=34%, median batch=3
  batch distribution: 60% small (<=4), 25% mid(5-12), 15% large(>12)
  observation: prefill improves KV-hit quickly and reduces extreme p99 by ~36%. Slight increase median due to extra work prepping prefill but within tolerance.

- Treatment B (prefill=2048, soft_hold=40ms):
  p50=52ms, p95=140ms, p99=310ms, kv-hit=66%, median batch=6
  tokens/sec increased by ~12% because fewer KV cache misses; observed occasional 300–800ms spikes tied to background cache-eviction GC.
  downside: higher memory and increased latency for non-burst steady traffic during cache prep windows.

- Treatment C (prefill=512, soft_hold=10ms, drain=0.8):
  p50=49ms, p95=150ms, p99=360ms, kv-hit=39%, median batch=3
  note: small drain-rate slow down flattens encoder spikes but reduces throughput headroom by ~6% — acceptable in Dedicated when headroom isn't fully used.

Small ascii trend snapshot (p99 relative to baseline for shear pulse):
Baseline |==================| (780)
A       |==========        | (500)
B       |====              | (310)
C       |=====             | (360)

Interpretation / rough thresholds:
- Prefill_budget around 500–2000 tokens is the key lever. 512 seems a good start for default Dedicated pools; 2048 gives stronger smoothing but costs memory and occasional GC-induced spikes.
- Soft_hold around 10–40ms helps batches coalesce (especially at client fanout 80–200), but above ~50ms it starts to hurt p50 for steady traffic.
- Drain_rate reductions help tail but steal throughput headroom; useful as an emergency dial or for low-utilization pools.

Open questions / weirdness seen:
- Why GC spikes correlate with large prefill runs? Hypothesis: prefill allocates larger KV entries that trigger allocator heuristics -> background compaction. Need to instrument allocator metrics (jemalloc stats) and compare across runs.
- Interaction with continuous batching: when many flows have small prompts, soft_hold is beneficial; for long prompts soft_hold doesn't matter (batch sizes already high).
- Multi-tenant effects: experiments were single-tenant; want to re-run with light background traffic to see interference on kv-hit and GC behavior.

Immediate recommendations (ops-readable):
- Add a new default config for Dedicated-devpool: prefill_budget_tokens=512, soft_hold_ms=10, drain_rate_factor=1.0. Mark as opt-in with a rollout metric: track p99 and kv-hit over 48h.
- Add a monitoring alert: sudden drop in kv-hit + rising p99 within 15m -> trigger automated partial rollback to prefill=0.
- For high-memory hosts consider prefill=2048 as a per-customer opt-in for latency-sensitive apps; warn about GC spikes.

Planned next experiments (short list):
- Repeat the same matrix but with multi-tenant background noise (10% baseline qps).
- Run jemalloc/tcmalloc profiling for 1h during prefill=2048 runs to capture alloc patterns.
- Try an adaptive prefill controller: grow prefill budget if arrival rate variance > threshold for last 500ms. Small control loop sim in Python first.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add traced logs for KV eviction timestamps (trace id + event) — file: /ops/traces/kv-evict-correlation.log
- Share summary with Maya + SRE team; propose a short playbook PR for Dedicated rollout.
- Link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/582 (draft heuristics implemented)

References / links I used while thinking: 
- JIRA-ENG-3241 (epic for microburst handling)
- small writeup: confluence:cap-surge-sim-2025 (simulation notes)

Hand-off summary (2 lines):
- Start with prefill=512 + soft_hold=10ms on low-util Dedicated pools. Monitor kv-hit and p99 closely. If p99 improves and no GC spikes, consider expanding to additional pools or experimenting with adaptive prefill controller.

Random stray ideas (brain dump):
- Could call this the "token-capacitor" feature in PRs to make concept memorable.
- Maybe combine with prefix-rewriting: prefill predicted prefixes only (not whole prompt) to reduce memory footprint.

End of scratchpad.
